newsitem.title: UK: Bloody milestones on road to IRA truce call.
newsitem.headline: Bloody milestones on road to IRA truce call.

text.p: The IRA was urged by its political wing, Sinn Fein, on Friday to call a new ceasefire in its 28-year war to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
The last IRA ceasefire was called on August 31, 1994, and lasted for 17 months. It ended on February 9, 1996, when a bomb hit London's Docklands, killing two people and injuring many more.
The blast signalled the start of a new wave of bombings and killings:
February 15, 1996 - Bomb left in a telephone box in central London is disarmed.
February 18 - IRA man Edward O'Brien killed by his own bomb on a bus in central London.
April 24 - Two devices were placed on Hammersmith Bridge in west London. The detonators went off, but the bombs did not explode.
June 15 - IRA explode huge bomb in city of Manchester, injuring 200 people.
June 28 - Three mortar bombs fired at British army barracks in Osnabrueck, Germany.
July 13 - Car-bomb hits hotel at Enniskillen, Northern Ireland, injuring 17 people, following a week of rioting after Protestant Orange March in Portadown.
July 15 - London police recover parts for 36 bombs.
September 23 - IRA suspect Diarmuid O'Neil shot dead by police during raids in London and southern England.
October 7 - IRA bomb attack on British army barracks near Belfast. One soldier killed and 31 people injured.
December 20 - Nigel Dodds of the pro-British Democratic Unionist Party narrowly escapes assassination by two gunmen while visiting his son at Belfast hospital.
December 21 - Leading republican Eddie Copeland injured after bomb explodes under his car in Belfast.
February 12 - British soldier Stephen Restorick shot dead by an IRA sniper at a Northern Ireland checkpoint.
March 23 - IRA escape bid foiled when a tunnel is discovered in Belfast's Maze Prison.
March 26 - IRA detonate two bombs on railway in northern England, bringing chaos to the network.
March 30 - Pro-British Loyalists plant car bomb outside Sinn Fein office in Belfast.
April 3 - British police find two bombs on motorway in northern England.
April 5 - IRA force the postponement of Grand National horse race at Aintree with bomb threats.
April 10 - Police reservist Alice Collins shot in the back by IRA sniper in Londonderry.
April 18 - Explosion and a series of telephoned coded bomb warnings caused travel chaos in England.
April 21 - London brought to near standstill after a series of bomb threats.
April 25 - Two explosions hit British motorway and a bomb warning forces closure of an airport.
April 29 - More rush-hour security alerts bring chaos to motorways in South east England.
May 9 - Off-duty police officer shot dead in a crowded Belfast gay bar by republican gunmen.
June 16 - Prime Minister Tony Blair bans contact between government officials and Sinn Fein after IRA shoot two policmen.
July 6 - Decision to force through Orange Order march at Portadown sparks two nights of shootings and rioting in nationalist areas across Northern Ireland.
July 10 - Orange Order eases tension by cancelling contentious marches through nationalist areas.
